title: Company-wide policies and processes (Access, Change, Data, Procurement, Vendors, Travel, Templates)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview
This page consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and internal templates. The goal is to provide a single, maintainable reference for employees and managers responsible for governance and day-to-day operations.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors who access corporate systems or handle company data.
- Excludes tactical team-level runbooks unless explicitly referenced.

Governance and ownership
- Policy owner: People Operations (people-ops) for process and approvals.
- Security owner: Security & Compliance for technical controls and reviews.
- Finance owner: Finance & Legal for procurement, vendor contracts, and expense policy.
- Review cadence: Annual review by owners; ad-hoc updates for regulatory or operational changes.

1) Access & permissions
Principles
- Least privilege by default.
- Role-based access control (RBAC) for production systems.
- Separation of duties for procurement, deployment, and billing.

Roles and standard access levels (table)
- Role: Viewer - Description: Read-only dashboards and non-sensitive documentation - Typical systems: Confluence (view), Grafana (view).
- Role: Contributor - Description: Write access to non-prod systems, documentation - Typical systems: GitHub (repo contributor), staging clusters.
- Role: Operator - Description: Deploy and operational ownership in prod with monitored approval - Typical systems: CI/CD, infra consoles.
- Role: Admin - Description: Full access with multi-factor auth and approval - Typical systems: IAM admin, cloud account owner.

Onboarding & offboarding
1. New hire access request: manager submits Access Request form (link to template in templates section).
2. People-ops approves role and notifies Security for privileged access.
3. Access is provisioned using Identity Provider (Okta) and audited nightly.
4. Offboarding: manager initiates offboard in HRIS; access revoked within 2 hours for terminated employees, within 48 hours for standard offboards.

Privileged access and emergency access
- Privileged access requires documented business justification, manager approval, and a 4-week automatic review.
- Emergency access (break-glass) must be requested via Escalation channel, logged in the emergency-access register, and reviewed within 72 hours.

2) Change management
Purpose
- Ensure production changes are low-risk, traceable, and reversible.

Change types
- Standard: Pre-approved low-risk changes (routine infra patching).
- Normal: Changes requiring testing and approval, scheduled during maintenance windows.
- Emergency: Changes required to remediate a live incident.

Approval matrix (summary)
- Low risk (Standard) - Approver: Service Owner.
- Medium risk (Normal) - Approver: Service Owner + Change Advisory Board (CAB) review.
- High risk (Prod-impacting) - Approver: Service Owner + CAB + Head of Eng or designated executive.

Change process (numbered)
1. Submit a Change Request (CR) with description, rollback plan, test plan, and stakeholders.
2. Triage by Service Owner and Security if change touches sensitive data or IAM.
3. CAB review (weekly) for Normal/High risk changes.
4. Schedule in maintenance window; notify affected teams 72 hours prior.
5. Execute, monitor, and record outcomes.
6. Post-change verification and close CR with runbook updates if needed.

Emergency changes
- Follow incident response runbook: emergency CR created post facto with supporting evidence.
- All emergency changes require retrospective and RCA within 5 business days.

3) Data management
Data classification
- Public: information intended for public consumption.
- Internal: default classification for non-sensitive documents.
- Restricted: PII, customer data, or regulatory data requiring controls.
- Regulated: Data subject to external regulatory controls (e.g., EU healthcare, financial).

Handling requirements
- Encryption at rest and in transit for Restricted and Regulated data (TLS 1.2+, AES-256).
- Access to Restricted/Regulated data requires explicit role assignment and justification.
- Logging and audit trails must be retained per retention policy.

Retention and deletion
- Default retention: 7 years for finance/legal records, 1 year for non-critical logs unless otherwise specified.
- Data deletion requests: Processed within 30 days; Security & Legal triage for regulatory holds.

Backups and recovery
- Daily backups for critical databases with monthly restore tests.
- RPO target: 4 hours for critical services; RTO target: 6 hours.

Data sharing and exports
- All exports of Restricted/Regulated data require a data export request and Security approval.
- Third-party transfers must be accompanied by a DPA and vendor security questionnaire.

4) Procurement & expenses
Procurement thresholds and approvals (summary)
- <$1,000 - Manager approval.
- $1,000–$25,000 - Department head approval.
- >$25,000 - Procurement + Finance + Legal review and contract.

Procurement process (high level)
1. Raise an RFC (Request for Commerce) with business justification, budget code, and preferred vendor.
2. Procurement team assesses vendor fit and negotiates T&Cs.
3. Purchase Order (PO) issued by Finance.
4. Receipt validation and invoice routing for payment.

Expense reimbursements
- Employees submit expenses within 30 days with receipts via Expense tool.
- Travel expenses follow the Travel section rules; per diem allowed only with manager pre-approval.
- Non-compliant expenses may be rejected by Finance.

5) Vendor management
Vendor lifecycle
- Vendor identification and business need.
- Security & privacy questionnaire and risk assessment.
- Contracting and SLAs (Finance & Legal).
- Ongoing monitoring, quarterly reviews for high-risk vendors.

Onboarding checklist
- Business justification and owner.
- Completed vendor security questionnaire.
- DPA signed for vendors processing Restricted/Regulated data.
- Assigned vendor liaison and access expiry dates.

Risk tiers and controls
- Low: SaaS tools with no access to restricted data (quarterly review).
- Medium: Tools with limited access to internal data (monthly review, least-privilege access).
- High: Vendors with access to Restricted/Regulated data (quarterly security attestations, annual SOC2 or equivalent).

Offboarding vendors
- Revoke credentials and API keys within 24 hours of contract end.
- Confirm data return or verified deletion per contract.

6) Travel policies
General rules
- Business travel must be approved in advance by the employee's manager.
- Employees should book economy travel unless otherwise approved for role-specific reasons.

Booking and expenses
- Use company travel booking tool or approved vendor.
- Hotel reasonable room rate; exceptions require manager justification.
- Meals reimbursed with itemized receipts; per diem options available for multi-day travel with pre-approval.

Safety and emergencies
- Employees must register travel to high-risk regions through People Ops.
- Emergency assistance: travel assistance provider information available in Travel template.

7) Internal templates and forms
Available templates (links are Confluence page names / templates)
- Access Request template - Use for onboarding and privilege changes.
- Change Request template - Standard CR submission form with rollback and test plans.
- Vendor Security Questionnaire - Standard security & privacy form for vendors.
- Procurement RFC - Request form for purchases and vendor engagements.
- Expense reimbursement template - Expense submission checklist and example receipts.
- Travel booking & pre-approval form - Pre-trip approvals and risk acknowledgment.

Usage guidelines
- Templates must be completed and attached to any request that moves through procurement, security review, or change management.

Audit, compliance, and training
- Quarterly audits of access lists and vendor inventory.
- Annual compliance training mandatory for all staff (includes change mgmt, data handling, and procurement basics).
- Executive summaries of audit findings routed to Board Audit Committee as required.

Metrics and SLOs (examples)
- Access provisioning SLA: 95% of standard requests completed within 48 hours.
- Offboarding SLA: 95% revoked within 2 hours for terminated employees.
- Change success rate: Target 99.5% for Standard changes; every high-risk change requires a documented rollback.

Escalation contacts and ownership
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.com (policy owner, onboarding/offboarding).
- Security: security@redwood.com (access audits, vendor assessments).
- Finance: finance@redwood.com (procurement, invoices).
- Tactical: Use on-call rotation for emergency changes (see eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts).

Related pages and references
- RBAC and IAM standards: /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth
- Change Advisory Board SOP: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/cab-sop
- Vendor risk matrix: /confluence/finance-and-legal/vendor-risk-matrix
